Subject: APAC1: Staged control-plane maintenance & KV-cache preservation (June 1-3)

Hi Rebecca and team,

Heads up — Redwood will perform a staged control-plane harmonization in the APAC1 region starting June 1 at 22:00 SGT (UTC+8) and continuing in low-traffic windows through June 3. This maintenance bundles a rolling driver/kernel harmonization with an opt-in KV-cache preservation workflow for customers that maintain long-lived sessions or affinity pins.

Why this matters: over the last quarter we've seen a small class of infrequent cold-cache tails after platform-level driver swaps. The harmonization reduces those tails and aligns kernel/driver stacks across hosts to prevent degraded inference tails during peak sequence lengths. For most customers there will be no visible impact. For a small percentage of long-lived, affinity-bound requests you may see brief connection recycling (sub-2s reconnects) or short-lived latency spikes during a particular host's switchover window.

What we're offering:
- Default path (no action required): We will perform rolling restarts with automatic graceful fallback. Most workloads will be unaffected.
- Opt-in warm-up (recommended for customers with pinned sessions / persistent KV usage): We can run a KV-cache prefetch and session warm-up for your tenancy to preserve state across restarts. This reduces any user-visible reconnects but requires a short pre-maintenance window (30–45 minutes) where we run warm-up traffic against your pinned model endpoints.

Requested action: please reply to this thread by EOD PT June 1 to confirm whether LambdaHealth would like to opt into the warm-up workflow. If you opt in, we will schedule the warm-up in the hour before your region's first restart window and share a DocuSign opt-in confirmation (attachment and link included).

Attachments: maintenance runbook (high level) and an opt-in PDF to sign if you choose warm-up.

If you have strict blackout windows or any compliance requirements that prevent warm-up traffic, let us know and we will exclude your tenancy from that step and rely on the default graceful fallback. We will publish a short post-maintenance summary and any relevant perf telemetry within 48 hours of completion.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Technical Account Manager
Redwood Inference

Rebecca — short answers here, and we'll follow up with the runbook page that calls this out explicitly:
- Warm-up traffic is synthetic (we replay non-PHI, randomized model prompts generated from safe templates). We will not send customer data or PHI during warm-up. We'll provide the template set for review before the warm-up window.
- LambdaHealth tenancy is scheduled for the APAC1 window starting June 2 02:00 SGT (UTC+8) local host swap; warm-up would begin ~01:15 SGT and last ~30 minutes.
- Fail-safes: if any abnormal error rates or latency regressions are detected during warm-up we will immediately abort warm-up and proceed with default graceful fallback (no warm-up). We also have a rollback play to pin traffic away from nodes being rotated.

Action items for Redwood ops (assigned):
- Marissa: prepare synthetic template set and share by EOD Jun 1.
- Grace: enable prefetched KV warm-up flag for LambdaHealth tenancy and reserve warm-up slot Jun 2 01:15–01:45 SGT.
- Neha: monitor canary metrics and stand by to abort if error rate > 0.5% above baseline.

Rebecca — if that sounds good, reply with a one-line opt-in and we'll send the DocuSign link for the opt-in notice and attach the runbook.
